tickets.subject: Bulldog tee
tickets.short_outcome: Tee was out of stock and vendor 1 was blocked by an unpaid invoice. After a human paid that invoice, Inventory got a vendor quote and placed its own restock order (no human approval needed for that, since it moves no cash) and the ticket closed as resolved.

agent_contributions.boss: Triaged the ticket, delegated to Inventory/Accounting/Customer Service across 5 runs, and made every status call (pending_human_approval -> blocked x2 -> pending_human_approval -> resolved).
agent_contributions.inventory: Found 0 on hand (shortfall 1), identified vendor 1 (Bulldog Print Co) and that it was blocked by invoice 501, later quoted $8/unit once given a pricing tool, and placed restock order (new invoice #502, $8, due 2026-09-14).
agent_contributions.accounting: Confirmed invoice 501's amount/overdue status and that cash was sufficient to pay it; later confirmed the invoice was paid and nothing further was due.
agent_contributions.facilities: Not delegated to -- no lease involved.
agent_contributions.customer_service: Drafted a cautious, no-date-promised reply to the requester (Tauhid Zaman) explaining the tee was out of stock; draft was recorded in ticket notes, never sent.

human_approvals.reason: Unblocks vendor 1 so a restock can be ordered.
Paid early (before its due date) to re-unblock vendor 1 for ticket 103, which shares the same vendor.

tickets.subject: Rent due
tickets.short_outcome: Rent on lease 1 was due in 2 days. A human approved payment, which rolled the lease's next due date forward a month; a re-run confirmed nothing further was owed and closed the ticket.

agent_contributions.boss: Delegated to Facilities then Accounting across 2 runs; set pending_human_approval, then resolved after re-verifying post-payment.
agent_contributions.inventory: Not delegated to -- no sku involved.
agent_contributions.accounting: Confirmed the $3,400 starting balance covered the $2,400 rent; on re-run confirmed the $152 remaining balance and that no payment was currently due.
agent_contributions.facilities: Looked up lease 1: $2,400/month, due 2026-09-02 (2 days out, urgent); on re-run confirmed the new due date (2026-10-02, 32 days out, no longer urgent).
agent_contributions.customer_service: Not delegated to -- an internal rent notice, no customer-facing reply needed.

human_approvals.reason: Rent was due in 2 days; shop had sufficient funds at the time.

tickets.subject: Bulk hoodie discount
tickets.short_outcome: Fulfillment became possible (vendor unblocked, $22/unit quote in hand), but the ticket never specified what discount the requester actually wants, so Accounting cannot evaluate an override. This is the ticket's genuine final state -- it needs a human to propose a specific discount percentage, which is a pricing judgment call our payment-approval mechanism isn't built to grant.

agent_contributions.boss: Delegated to Accounting/Inventory/Customer Service across 4 runs; correctly caught a vendor-invoice collision with ticket 101 (set blocked), then re-verified after that invoice was paid.
agent_contributions.inventory: Confirmed 8 of 20 on hand (shortfall 12); found vendor 1 blocked first by invoice 501, then later by ticket 101's own invoice #502; quoted $22/unit once both were cleared and vendor 1 was unblocked.
agent_contributions.accounting: Repeatedly and correctly reported it could not evaluate the requested discount without a target price or percentage -- the ticket itself never supplies one.
agent_contributions.facilities: Not delegated to -- no lease involved.
agent_contributions.customer_service: Drafted an unsent reply to Yale AI Club asking them to specify the discount they're requesting, with no price or fulfillment promised.

human_approvals.reason: Shared with ticket 101 -- paid to re-unblock vendor 1 for this ticket's hoodie restock.

tickets.known_limitation: No backend action exists for a human to approve a discount/price override (only pay_invoice/pay_lease exist). A human would need to decide on a discount percentage outside this system and communicate it back before Accounting could finalize the override.

system_fixes_made_during_this_run.issue: Inventory had no tool to look up a SKU's unit cost, so it could never actually call create_restock_order (which requires one) no matter how many times it re-checked the vendor.
system_fixes_made_during_this_run.fix: Added get_pricing to Inventory's toolset in backend/agents.py; documented in backend/prompts/inventory.md.

system_fixes_made_during_this_run.issue: Boss treated placing a restock order (which moves no cash) as needing the same human-approval gate as an actual payment, with no corresponding approval action available anywhere in the system -- an unresolvable deadlock.
system_fixes_made_during_this_run.fix: Clarified backend/prompts/boss.md: only payments (invoice/lease) require human approval; Boss may authorize a restock order itself.
